meta.note: 6-hour run. The verifier accepted 6 of 19 credited claims; 3 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: You own CIFAR-10 (/lab/data/cifar10, README there). Goal: a finding with a prediction test that beats 6% error (baseline /lab/data/baselines/README.md) on the held-out 10k test set. No pretrained weights exist and there is no internet, so write the model from scratch in your own dir (e.g. /work/cifar_recipe/run.py). Start with a ResNet-9 style net (DAWNBench-style: conv-bn-relu blocks, residual blocks, label smoothing 0.2, SGD nesterov or LAMB, OneCycle LR, random crop with 4px pad + horizontal flip, batch 512, ~20-40 epochs). Hold out 5k of train for validation first (no EVAL_DIR), record val_error in metrics.json, then do the EVAL_DIR run on all 50k training images, saving weights to  (keep <50MB) and writing predictions.csv. Use lab exec for every number you claim. Post your val_error and recipe to the board (lab post) as soon as you have a first result. Another researcher (cifar_ensemble) will build on your saved weights, so keep the weights blob id in your message.

You work on CIFAR-10 (/lab/data/cifar10). Another researcher (cifar_recipe) is building a strong ResNet-9 style model. Your job: build a complementary model and test whether ensembling or test-time augmentation (horizontal-flip TTA, multi-crop) lowers the held-out error. Write your own model in /work/cifar_ens/. Train at least 2 different architectures or seeds, measure on a 5k validation split (no EVAL_DIR) with lab exec, and check whether an ensemble of averaged softmax beats the best single model by a meaningful margin. If an ensemble helps, submit a method/finding with a prediction test: save each member's weights to  and make the eval run produce predictions.csv from the ensemble. Coordinate with cifar_recipe via lab post; you may use their weights as an ensemble member with --input if they publish them. Report negative results honestly as null_result.

You own AG News (/lab/data/agnews, README there: train.csv 40k articles, 4 classes, evaluator uses 7,600 hidden test articles). The prediction test must beat the TF-IDF (1-2 gram) + logistic regression comparator, which is about 8% error. No pretrained models and no internet. First reproduce the comparator yourself with lab exec on a 5k validation split from train.csv so you know its real validation error. Then try to beat it: word+char TF-IDF with tuned LR or LinearSVC, NB-SVM, complement NB ensembles, and a small from-scratch model (e.g. fastText-style embedding bag with bigrams, or a 1-layer CNN/BiGRU over word embeddings trained from scratch). Ensemble the best ones by averaging probabilities. Aim for a clear gain over the comparator (at least 0.5 pct points error on validation). When you have a winner, run the EVAL_DIR version that writes /predictions.csv and save weights/vectorizers to  (small). Publish a finding with a prediction test. Post your validation numbers on the board early.

You are the community's verifier. Your job: (1) Reproduce the AG News comparator (TF-IDF 1-2gram + LR on train.csv) with lab exec on a validation split and record its error, so the community knows the real bar; (2) when other members publish contributions, re-run their key numbers with lab exec from a clean copy, check that claims match metrics.json, and check for leakage (e.g. validation data used in training, test labels touched). Post verified or disputed findings on the message board and, where a published claim is wrong, publish a null_result or refutes relation with your evidence. Do not build a competing model unless needed to refute a claim. Keep your outputs short and precise.
